name: Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy (PSRT)
founders: Michael W. Donnino, MD (BIDMC/Harvard; emergency medicine and critical care; PI and co-instructor)
Patricia (Patty) Howard, BS (BIDMC; mind-body co-instructor; no clinical licence stated)
Howard Schubiner, MD (acknowledged consultant and instructor trainer; not an author)
founded_year_range: 2014-2021: first BIDMC 'Mind Body Syndrome (MBS) Therapy' pilot started Feb 2014, registered Apr 2014 (NCT02117921); 'PSRT' name first published 2021
category: psychological/neuroplastic-pain therapy (academic research protocol, Sarno lineage)
cost_summary: No direct cost. PSRT is a research protocol, free to trial participants and not available commercially or clinically (BIDMC, 2021). Funded by philanthropy: Adam D'Angelo for the pilot; D'Angelo and James O'Shaughnessy for the long COVID study.
mechanisms: neuroplastic/learned pain (brain-generated danger signal / predictive processing)
mechanism_summary: Nonspecific symptoms (back pain, post-COVID fatigue, dyspnea, brain fog) are treated as psychophysiologic: CNS-mediated somatic expressions of stress, repressed emotion and underlying conflict, following Sarno. They are kept going by a classical-conditioning-like link between neutral triggers (bending, sitting, exertion) and symptoms, and by fear and avoidance; reduced pain anxiety statistically mediated the benefit. The same model is applied across conditions after medical screening excludes organic disease; only the trigger targets differ.
techniques: psychophysiologic pain education (Sarno's Healing Back Pain, Schubiner's Unlearn Your Pain)
symptom-history review aimed at accepting psychological origin
visual motor imagery of triggering activities as proof and as desensitization (imaginal exposure)
expressive writing and journaling (EAET-style emotional awareness and expression)
full 8-9 week MBSR course (body scan, breath awareness, sitting meditation, 6-hour retreat day)
anxiety workbook (The Mindful Way Through Anxiety)
mainstream_notes: Research-only protocol at Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Harvard) with Brigham & Women's pain psychologists. Published in mainstream journals (Pain Reports, J Pain Res, Mayo Clin Proc IQO, Front Pain Res), but no clinical service, guideline mention, training program or dissemination was found.
insurance_notes: Not offered as a billable service. Delivered free within trials.

key_trials.citation: Donnino MW, Thompson GS, Mehta S, Paschali M, Howard P, et al. Psychophysiologic symptom relief therapy for chronic back pain: a pilot randomized controlled trial. Pain Rep. 2021;6(3):e959. PMID 34589642
key_trials.design: Pilot 3-arm RCT (PSRT vs MBSR vs usual care), partially blinded (PSRT arm unblinded), single site, developer-run; NCT04039139
key_trials.finding: Roland-Morris disability fell from 9.5 to 3.3 at 26 weeks with PSRT, superior to MBSR (p=0.04) and usual care (p=0.03); 63.6% (7/11) pain-free at 26 weeks vs 25.0% and 16.7%.

key_trials.citation: Pester BD, Yamin JB, Cabrera MJ, et al. Change in pain-related anxiety mediates the effects of PSRT on pain disability for chronic back pain: secondary results from a randomized controlled trial. J Pain Res. 2023;16:3871-3880. PMID 38026456
key_trials.design: Secondary/mediation analysis of the pilot RCT
key_trials.finding: More PSRT patients achieved >=75% disability reduction at all time points; reduced pain anxiety (PASS-20) mediated the 26-week disability effect.

key_trials.citation: Donnino M, Howard P, Mehta S, et al. Psychophysiologic Symptom Relief Therapy (PSRT) for Post-acute Sequelae of COVID-19. Mayo Clin Proc Innov Qual Outcomes. 2023;7(4):337-348. PMID 37361483
key_trials.design: Single-arm, uncontrolled virtual interventional cohort; PASC >=12 weeks without organ injury, age 18-60; NCT04854772
key_trials.finding: SSS-8 somatic symptoms fell by 8.5, 9.4 and 10.9 points at 4, 8 and 13 weeks (p<.001); fatigue, dyspnea and pain also improved. No control group and no follow-up beyond 13 weeks.

key_trials.citation: NCT04689646, Mind Body Syndrome Therapy for Chronic Pain (BIDMC; PI Donnino); rationale in Paschali M et al. Front Pain Res 2024;5:1328495 (PMID 39091382)
key_trials.design: 3-arm RCT (two mind-body interventions vs usual care), started May 2021
key_trials.finding: Completed 2026-07-06; no results posted or published as of Oct 2026.

controversy: Long COVID and ME/CFS communities (e.g. S4ME) object to recasting post-COVID fatigue and dyspnea as conditioned or psychophysiologic, and to encouraging exertion. Methodological critiques: tiny samples (11 in the PSRT arm), partial blinding, self-report outcomes alongside an explicit goal of persuading patients their symptoms are psychological, selection of participants open to mind-body treatment, unequal treatment hours (38 vs 22), the same two instructors throughout, and an uncontrolled long COVID cohort. All trials are developer-run. The authors concede that benefit does not prove the psychophysiologic premise.

indicators.metric: Earliest trial registration (as 'Mind Body Syndrome Therapy')
indicators.value: NCT02117921, start Feb 2014, completed Dec 2016, no results
BIDMC release syndicated via Newswise; later NICABM blog coverage
~100-150 (35 + 23 + 126 + up to 20 in early pilot; PSRT recipients fewer)
One S4ME thread (June 2026, 13 posts); TMS Wiki forum search for 'Donnino' returned no threads; Reddit not accessible

popularity.reach_estimate: About 100-150 people enrolled across trials (of whom perhaps 75-100 received PSRT); perhaps 10^3-10^4 reached indirectly through press coverage and citations. There is no consumer channel.
popularity.method_notes: There is no website, app, book or social presence, so the trajectory follows research activity: trial registrations (2014, 2019, 2020-2021), the pilot publication and BIDMC press release (2021 peak), the long COVID preprint/paper and mediation paper (2022-2023), the rationale paper (2024) and completion of the large RCT (2026). Reach is the sum of trial enrollments. Citation counts are from the Europe PMC API (re-verified 2026-10-13). TMS Wiki forum search found no threads; Reddit blocked automated access and Google Trends was not collected (term too rare); activity levels are coarse judgments.
